The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the respondents to pay appropriate compensation to the petitioner in terms with the award dated 20.10.2020 (Annexure-4 to the writ petition) passed by the respondent no. 6 in Arbitration Case No. 30 of 2020, whereby the said respondent, after considering the entire records of the case as well as taking into account the enquiry report of the respondent no. 5 and after due consideration of the enquiry report of the Circle Officer, Dhanabd, has directed the respondent nos. 2 and 5 to pay compensation to the petitioner for acquisition of his land and structure situated at Khata No. 5, Plot No. 157 (New Khata No. 58, New Plot No. 185), Mouza-Khudandih, Thana No. 242, measuring an area of 43 decimals approx. for the purpose of expansion/broadening of NH-32 (Rajabhita/Rajganj to Lohapitti Section) at market rate Mukesh Kumar Choudhary vs National Highways Authority Of India on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58683666/
1 treating the same as residential land.

sentences.text:
Further prayer has been made for issuance of direction upon the respondent nos. 4 & 5 to pay the compensation amount along with appropriate interest from the date of acquisition of the said land till the date of its payment after deducting the amount of Rs.3,43,647.20, which was illegally calculated by the respondent no. 5 @ Rs.3,82,000/- per acre i.e.,
Rs.3,820/- per decimal for the total acquired land and was paid to the petitioner against compensation of the said land, however, the same was accepted by him under protest.

2. The respondent nos. 1 and 2 initially filed a counter affidavit on 14.12.2022 stating that the respondent no. 6 had exceeded his jurisdiction by remanding the matter to the respondent no. 5 instead of determining the compensation on his own as contemplated under Section 3-G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act, 1956").

3. The writ petition was taken up on 24.07.2023 and on the said date, on putting a question to learned counsel for the respondent nos. 1 and 2 as to whether the said respondents had challenged the award dated 20.10.2020 passed by the respondent no. 6 in Arbitration Case No. 30 of 2020, it was replied by learned counsel for the said respondents that the same was not challenged till that date.

4. It was thus observed by this Court in its order dated 24.07.2023 that the stand taken in the counter affidavit regarding the respondent no. 6 exceeding his jurisdiction by remanding the matter to the respondent no. 5 instead of determining the compensation on his own as contemplated under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956, had no relevance.
It was further observed that if at all the respondent nos. 1 and 2 were aggrieved with the said award, they should have challenged the same as provided under law.
The Court also deprecated the approach of the respondent nos.1 and 2 due to which an awardee was compelled to seek remedy under extraordinary writ jurisdiction.

In the said circumstance, the respondent nos. 4 and 5 were directed to file counter affidavit explaining as to why the award dated 20.10.2020 passed by the respondent no. 6 in the said arbitration proceeding was not implemented.
The case was again taken up on 10.08.2023, however, the respondent nos. 4 and 5 failed to file counter affidavit.
The Court again deprecated the approach of the said respondents and granted one week's more time to file counter affidavit by way of last indulgence.

5. The writ petition was thereafter taken up on 23.08.2023 and on the said date, following order was passed:
"It is relevant to note that the present writ petition was filed on 29.09.2022 for issuance of direction upon the respondents to pay appropriate compensation to the petitioner in terms with the award dated 20.10.2020 (Annexure-4 to the writ petition) passed by the respondent No.6 in Arbitration Case No. 30/2020.
Subsequently, the writ petition was taken up on 24.07.2023 & 10.08.2023.

Since no counter affidavit was filed on behalf of the respondent Nos. 4 & 5, while deprecating such attitude of the said respondents vide order dated 10.08.2023, they were given one week's more time by way of last indulgence to file the counter affidavit.

sentences.text:
Pursuant to the order dated 10.08.2023, a counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent Nos. 4 & 5, paragraph 5 of which reads as under:
"5. That the requisitioning department through the Project Director NHAI (PIU)
Govindpur, Dhanbad namely the respondent No.2 has intimated vide email dated 19.08.2023 at 14.32 hrs. that Arbitration Case No. 10/2023, filing No. 982/2023 has already been filed against the petitioner/awardee dated 20.10.2020 in the competent Court of the Civil Judge, Sr. Div. No. 1st at Dhanbad.'' did not take any step within a reasonable time to challenge the award dated 20.10.2020 passed by the respondent No.6 in Arbitration Case No. 30/2020

, rather after filing of the writ petition and particularly after passing the aforesaid orders, they have chosen to file a petition invoking Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1996') challenging the said award passed by the respondent No.6.

Under the said circumstance, this Court is of the prima facie view that the respondent Nos. 1 & 2 have not only been negligent in taking appropriate recourse provided under law against the award dated 20.10.2020 passed by the respondent No.6, but have also tried to frustrate the case of the petitioner as well as to circumvent the aforesaid orders of this Court.
The said petition under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 appears to have been filed only to save the skin of the concerned authorities of the National Highways Authority of India.

However, since the respondent Nos. 1 & 2 have filed the counter affidavit only challenging the maintainability of the present writ petition, they are granted three weeks' more time to file a counter affidavit explaining the unreasonable delay committed by them in challenging the award dated 20.10.2020 passed by the respondent No.6 under Section 34 of the Act, 1996.

Put up this case on 18.09.2023 under the same heading."
6.

In pursuance of the aforesaid order dated 23.08.2023, another counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent nos. 1 and 2 on 16.09.2023, wherein the reasons for not preferring any application under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 challenging the award dated 20.10.2020 passed in Arbitration Case No. 30 of 2020, has been explained.

The relevant paragraphs of the said counter affidavit read as under:
5.

That on receipt of the copy of the award dated 20.10.2020 passed in Case No.
30/2020 by the ld.

Arbitrator, the answering respondent had sought legal opinion and after receipt of the same, issued instructions to its local counsel in Dhanbad vide letter dated 06.03.2021, to file an application challenging the said award under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act.

sentences.text: That however, owing to the pandemic, the said counsel was unwell for a very long time and failed to intimate the answering respondent that the said Section 34 application had not been filed by him.

7. That it was only when the answering respondent sought details of the case from the counsel vide its letter dated 14.08.2023, it came to the knowledge of the answering respondent that the counsel could not file the said application under Section 34 earlier.

8. That the said counsel through his letter dated 14.08.2023 has informed the answering respondent that owing to the pandemic, lockdown and file misplacement, the said application under Section 34 could not be filed earlier and that the said counsel is immediately taking steps to file the application.

9. That it is humbly stated and submitted that an application under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act has now been filed by the answering respondent on 19.08.2023 which is registered as Arbitration Case No. 10 of 2023 and is currently pending before the ld. Court of Civil Judge (Sr. Division)-I at Dhanbad for further adjudication."

entities.text: Court of Civil Judge (Sr. Division)-I at Dhanbad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the aforesaid facts stated in the counter affidavit particularly that the respondent nos. 1 and 2 have already preferred Arbitration Case No. 10 of 2023 challenging the award dated 20.10.2020 passed in Arbitration Case No. 30 of 2020, which is said to be pending in the court of Civil Judge (Sr. Division)-I, Dhanbad, this Court is not inclined to issue writ of mandamus to the concerned respondents for the present.
8. The writ petition is accordingly disposed of.
9. The parties are, however, at liberty to pursue their respective cases in Arbitration Case No. 10 of 2023.
